examples.en: A temporary building was put up next to the construction site.

examples.ko: 시장 한쪽에 가건물을 세워서 장사를 했어요.
examples.en: They set up a makeshift building at the edge of the market and sold goods.

examples.ko: 가건물은 튼튼하지 않아서 태풍이 오면 위험해요.
examples.en: Makeshift buildings aren't sturdy, so they're dangerous in a typhoon.

examples.ko: 학교를 고치는 동안 가건물에서 수업을 했어요.
examples.en: We had classes in a temporary building while the school was being repaired.

examples.ko: 행사장 앞에 있던 가건물도 곧 없어질 거예요.
examples.en: The temporary building in front of the event site will also be gone soon.
I was surprised that the temporary office was warmer than I expected.

explain: 오래 쓰려고 튼튼하게 지은 게 아니라 임시로 지은 건물이에요. 공사장 사무실, 임시 매장, 행사장 건물에 많이 쓰고, 뉴스에서는 '불법 가건물'처럼 나오기도 해요. '임시 건물'이라고 풀어서도 말해요.
explain_en: It is a building put up temporarily, not built sturdily for long use. It is used for construction-site offices, temporary shops and event buildings, and in the news it appears as '불법 가건물' (illegal temporary building). People also say it more plainly as '임시 건물'.

examples.en: Passengers watched the sea from the deck.
Waves splashed up onto the deck.
The sailors scrubbed the deck clean.
If you go out onto the deck, the wind blows hard.

examples.ko: 크루즈 갑판은 저녁이 되면 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: The cruise ship's deck gets crowded in the evening.

examples.ko: 폭풍이 오기 전에 갑판의 짐을 묶었어요.
examples.en: Before the storm, they tied down the cargo on the deck.

explain: 배 위쪽에 바깥으로 드러난 넓은 바닥이라서 '갑판에 올라가다/나가다'처럼 말해요. 배 안의 방은 '선실'이라고 해서 갑판과 구별해요. 배가 크면 '갑판'이 여러 층일 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is the wide, open-air floor on top of a ship, so people say '갑판에 올라가다/나가다'. A room inside the ship is a '선실', which is different from the deck. A large ship can have several decks.

examples.ko: 이 마을 근처에 오래된 광산이 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old mine near this village.

examples.ko: 광산에서 일하는 사람들은 힘든 일을 해요.
examples.en: People who work in mines do hard work.
After the mine closed, people left.
That mine was famous for coal.
I was shocked to see the news about the mine accident.
The road to the mine is blocked.

explain: '탄광'은 석탄을 캐는 광산이고, 금광·은광처럼 캐는 것에 따라 이름이 달라져요. 지금은 문을 닫은 광산을 박물관이나 관광지로 쓰는 곳도 많아요.
explain_en: A '탄광' is a coal mine, and the name changes with what is dug, such as '금광' (gold mine) and '은광' (silver mine). Many closed mines are now used as museums or tourist spots.

examples.en: There are many bridges over the Han River.
The new bridge is scheduled to be completed next year.
The road is jammed because of the bridge construction.

examples.ko: 오래된 교량은 안전 점검을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Old bridges need safety inspections.
Once you cross this bridge, you are right in the city.

examples.ko: 밤이 되면 교량들은 조명이 켜져서 예뻐요.
examples.en: At night the bridges are lit up and look pretty.

explain: 일상에서는 '다리'가 훨씬 흔해요. '교량'은 공사, 뉴스, 안내문에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 사람이나 일이 둘 사이를 이어 줄 때 '교량 역할'이라고 비유해서도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 통역사가 두 회사의 교량 역할을 해요.
phrases.en: serve as a bridge between two sides
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 둘을 이어 주는 사람이나 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person or thing that connects two different sides.

explain_en: In daily life '다리' is far more common. '교량' is the formal word used in construction, news, and notices. It is also used figuratively, as in '교량 역할', for someone or something that connects two sides.

examples.ko: 요즘은 교통난 때문에 출근이 정말 힘들어요.
examples.en: These days commuting is really hard because of the traffic problems.
Traffic problems in big cities get worse every year.

examples.ko: 교통난을 줄이려고 버스 전용 차로를 늘렸어요.
examples.en: They added bus-only lanes to reduce traffic congestion.
Highway traffic is especially bad in the vacation season.

examples.ko: 교통난에 시달리다 보니 지하철을 타기로 했어요.
examples.en: After suffering from the traffic, I decided to take the subway.

examples.ko: 교통난만 아니면 회사 근처에 살 필요가 없을 텐데요.
examples.en: If it weren't for the traffic, I wouldn't need to live near work.

explain: 차가 막히는 것뿐 아니라 도로, 주차, 대중교통이 모자라서 생기는 도시의 교통 문제 전체를 말해요. 일상에서 막히는 길은 '교통 체증'이나 '차가 막히다'라고 해요. '주택난', '취업난'처럼 '-난'이 붙은 말과 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It covers not only jammed roads but the city's whole transport problem from shortages of roads, parking and public transit. In daily talk, a jammed road is '교통 체증' or '차가 막히다'. It is handy to learn it with other '-난' words like '주택난' and '취업난'.

examples.en: The road winds on and on.
We climbed up the winding mountain path.
The river winds through the fields.
My hair is wavy, so I straighten it every day.
I got lost in the winding alleys.
The snake slithered away in curves.

explain: 길, 강, 머리카락처럼 길쭉한 것이 이리저리 굽은 모양이에요. '구불구불하다'로도 쓰고, 길이 꼬불꼬불한 건 '꼬불꼬불'이 더 작고 촘촘한 느낌이에요. 곧은 모양은 '쭉' 또는 '똑바로'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes long things like roads, rivers and hair bending this way and that. It also works as '구불구불하다'. '꼬불꼬불' feels smaller and tighter, while straight shapes are '쭉' or '똑바로'.

examples.en: We're in the mountains, so there is no cell tower nearby.

examples.ko: 기지국이 고장 나서 전화가 안 터져요.
examples.en: The base station broke down, so phone calls won't connect.
A new cell tower was built and the internet got faster.
The carrier decided to build more base stations.

examples.ko: 기지국 근처에 살면 전파가 강하게 잡혀요.
examples.en: If you live near a cell tower, the signal is strong.

examples.ko: 건물 옥상에 기지국 안테나가 설치되어 있어요.
examples.en: A base station antenna is installed on the rooftop.

explain: 휴대폰 신호 이야기에서 '기지국'은 '전파가 터지다', '통신망'과 함께 나와요. 안테나 하나가 아니라 신호를 받아 전달하는 시설 전체를 가리켜서 '안테나'와는 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: In talk about phone signals, '기지국' goes with '전파가 터지다' (the signal comes through) and '통신망' (network). It means the whole facility that receives and relays signals, not just one antenna, so it is kept distinct from '안테나'.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 기찻길이 있어서 기차 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: There is a railroad in front of my house, so I can hear the trains.
When I was little, I walked along the railroad.
The railroad is dangerous, so you must not cross it.
A train passes slowly over the tracks.
The old railroad has been turned into a walking path.
I stopped for a moment at the railroad crossing.

explain: '철길'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. '철도'는 열차 교통 전체를 말할 때가 많고, '기찻길'은 열차가 다니는 길 그 자체를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '철길'. '철도' often refers to the whole railway system, while '기찻길' refers to the path the train runs on.

examples.en: The area near the landfill smells terrible.

examples.ko: 이 공항은 바다를 메운 매립지에 지었어요.
examples.en: This airport was built on land reclaimed from the sea.

examples.ko: 매립지가 꽉 차서 새 장소를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The landfill is full, so they are looking for a new site.
Families ride bikes in the landfill park.
The news is covering the landfill problem.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 줄이면 매립지로 가는 양이 줄어요.
examples.en: If we reduce trash, the amount going to landfills decreases.

explain: '쓰레기 매립지'로 가장 많이 듣고, 바다를 메워 만든 땅도 매립지라고 해요. 둘 다 흙이나 쓰레기로 메운 곳이라는 점이 같아요. 뉴스에서 환경 문제를 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: You hear it most in 쓰레기 매립지 (waste landfill), and land made by filling in the sea is also 매립지. Both are places filled in with soil or trash. It is common in environmental news.

examples.en: It rained a lot and the waterway got blocked.
The farmer made a water channel to the rice field.

examples.ko: 배는 좁은 물길을 따라 천천히 갔어요.
examples.en: The boat went slowly along the narrow waterway.
The sound of the stream coming from the mountain is refreshing.
The course of the water changed after the typhoon.
In the old days they carried goods by water route.

explain: '강'이나 '바다'처럼 이름이 있는 큰 물이 아니라, 물이 흘러가는 길 자체를 말해요. '물길을 내다', '물길이 막히다'처럼 써요. 땅 위의 길은 '길', 바다 위 길은 '뱃길'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the path water flows along, not a named river or sea. Common uses are 물길을 내다 and 물길이 막히다. A road on land is a 길, and a route over the sea is a 뱃길.

examples.en: When you board the bus, please tap your transit card.
I checked my ticket before boarding the train.
No one boards through the back door.
Passengers line up and board in order.
I got on at Seoul Station.

examples.ko: 승차할 때 아이 손을 꼭 잡으세요.
examples.en: Hold your child's hand tightly when boarding.

explain: 반대말은 '하차하다'예요. 안내 방송이나 표지판에서 많이 보이고, 말할 때는 '타다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '승차'는 탈것에 타는 일, 즉 버스·기차·택시 등에 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '하차하다' (get off). You see it on announcements and signs; in speech '타다' is far more natural. It is for vehicles like buses, trains and taxis.

examples.en: The waste collection area is behind the apartment building.
I gathered the trash and threw it away at the dump.

examples.ko: 동네 쓰레기장 냄새 때문에 창문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: I closed the window because of the smell from the neighborhood dump.
I heard a big dump opened next to the mountain.
This road leads to the dump.
Please keep the waste area clean.

explain: '쓰레기통'은 쓰레기를 담는 통이고, '쓰레기장'은 쓰레기를 모아 두거나 버리는 장소예요. 종류별로 나눠서 버리는 곳은 '분리수거장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A 쓰레기통 is a bin that holds trash, while a 쓰레기장 is a place where trash is gathered or dumped. A spot where recyclables are sorted by type is called a 분리수거장.

examples.ko: 급하다고 액셀을 너무 세게 밟지 마세요.
examples.en: Even if you are in a hurry, don't press the accelerator too hard.
In this car the accelerator is on the right.
Beginner drivers find it hard to control the accelerator.

examples.ko: 신호가 바뀌자 그가 액셀에서 발을 뗐어요.
examples.en: When the light changed, he took his foot off the accelerator.
The car stopped and I just kept pressing the accelerator.
You have to raise your speed with the accelerator on an uphill road.

explain: 자동차에서 속도를 올리는 페달은 '액셀', 속도를 줄이는 페달은 '브레이크'예요. '엑셀'은 컴퓨터 프로그램 이름으로 쓰는 말이라서 철자가 비슷해도 헷갈리면 안 돼요.
explain_en: In a car, the pedal that raises speed is the 액셀 and the pedal that slows you down is the 브레이크. 엑셀 is the spelling used for the computer program (Excel), so do not mix the two up even though they look similar.

examples.ko: 고속도로 요금소 앞에서 차가 많이 막혀요.
examples.en: Traffic is heavily jammed in front of the highway tollgate.
We passed through the tollgate in the Hi-Pass lane.

examples.ko: 다음 요금소까지 얼마나 더 가야 해요?
examples.en: How much farther is it to the next tollgate?
The tollgate staff told me the toll.
A rest stop appears right after the tollgate.
You can also pay by card at the tollgate.

explain: '톨게이트'라고 말하는 사람도 많아요. 요즘은 '하이패스' 차로로 멈추지 않고 지나가는 일도 있어요. '요금소를 지나다/통과하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Many people also say '톨게이트'. These days you can pass through a '하이패스' lane without stopping. It is used like '요금소를 지나다/통과하다'.

examples.en: The plane takes off in ten minutes.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 비행기가 이륙하지 못했어요.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the plane could not take off.
At the moment of takeoff, my ears feel blocked.

examples.ko: 비행기가 이륙한 지 한 시간쯤 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been about an hour since the plane took off.

examples.ko: 이륙할 때는 안전벨트를 꼭 매야 해요.
examples.en: You must fasten your seat belt when taking off.
They announced that the plane will take off soon once the fog clears.

explain: 비행기가 땅에서 떠오를 때 쓰고, 반대는 '착륙하다'예요. 사람이 공항에 도착하거나 떠나는 건 '도착하다', '출발하다'로 말해요. 헬리콥터나 우주선에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is for a plane lifting off the ground, and the opposite is 착륙하다. A person arriving at or leaving an airport is 도착하다 or 출발하다. It can also be used for helicopters and spacecraft.

examples.ko: 정면충돌 사고가 나서 길이 많이 막혀요.
examples.en: A head-on collision happened, so the road is heavily jammed.
Both cars were badly damaged in a head-on crash.
The two people's opinions came into direct conflict.
Let's avoid a head-on clash and solve it by talking.
Right before the head-on crash, the driver turned the wheel.
The union and the company are on the verge of a direct clash.

explain: 차가 앞에서 서로 부딪치는 사고에도 쓰고, 의견이나 입장이 크게 맞서는 것을 비유할 때도 써요. 뉴스에서는 '정면충돌 사고'와 '정면충돌 위기'를 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for cars hitting nose to nose and figuratively for opinions or positions clashing directly. In the news you often see '정면충돌 사고' (head-on crash) and '정면충돌 위기' (clash crisis).

examples.en: There are many tall buildings in central Seoul.

examples.ko: 도시 중심부까지 지하철로 십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes ten minutes by subway to reach the city center.
The wind is much stronger at the center of the typhoon.
The square is in the center of the village.

examples.ko: 이 사건의 중심부에는 한 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was one person at the heart of this case.
The closer you get to the center, the more expensive the housing becomes.

explain: '중심'은 한가운데 점이나 중요한 점을, '중심부'는 한가운데 넓은 부분을 가리켜요. '도시 중심부'처럼 면적이 있는 곳에 써요. 가운데 거리를 말하는 '시내', '도심'과 비슷하지만 '중심부'는 도시가 아닌 것에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '중심' is the middle point or what matters most, while '중심부' is a broad central region, as in '도시 중심부'. It resembles '시내' and '도심', but '중심부' also works for things that are not cities, like a typhoon.

p.n: 중심부 is the central area; 중심 sounds like a point.

examples.en: I went to watch at the drama set.
The filming location was crowded with people from morning.
The actor was reading the script at the set.

examples.ko: 촬영장 근처에서 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos near the set.
Our village was used as a movie location.
I met the director as soon as I arrived at the set.

explain: '촬영장'은 영화나 드라마를 찍는 곳이고, '촬영지'는 실제로 찍은 장소예요. 팬들은 드라마의 '촬영지'를 일부러 찾아가기도 해요.
explain_en: 촬영장 is the place where a film or drama is shot, while 촬영지 is the actual real-world place where scenes were filmed. Fans sometimes travel to a drama's 촬영지 on purpose.

examples.en: My grandfather worked in a coal mine when he was young.
This town used to be famous for its coal mines.

examples.ko: 탄광이 문을 닫은 뒤 사람들이 떠났어요.
examples.en: After the coal mine closed, people left.

examples.ko: 문 닫은 옛 탄광을 박물관으로 바꾼 곳이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a place where a closed old coal mine became a museum.
Everyone was worried by the news of the mine accident.

examples.ko: 강원도에는 탄광 지역이 많이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Many coal-mining areas remain in Gangwon Province.

explain: '광산'은 금, 은, 석탄 등을 캐는 곳을 모두 부르는 넓은 말이고, '탄광'은 그중 석탄만 캐는 곳이에요. 거기서 일하는 사람은 '광부'라고 해요. 강원도 같은 지역 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 광산 is the broad word for any mine that digs gold, silver, coal and so on, and 탄광 is the one that digs only coal. A person who works there is a 광부. It often comes up when talking about areas like Gangwon Province.
